name: item
description: A compact, repeatable list-row component for a single entry in a list, feed, or menu. Six leading Types, three container Variants, and three Sizes. Always use 'item' — never '_item-image' standalone.

item.purpose: Full list row — 6 Types × 3 Variants × 3 Sizes. Always use this.

_item-image.purpose: Image placeholder sub-component — assembled inside item. Never use standalone.

intent.Default: Text-only — no leading element. Simplest list row.
intent.Icon: 16×16 icon precedes content. Use for category/action rows.
intent.Avatar: 40×40 avatar precedes content. Use for people-centric lists.
intent.Image: 32×32 image thumbnail precedes content. Use for product/file/brand rows.
intent.Header: Full-width cover image above content row. Use for editorial/rich rows. No action-slot.
intent.Link: Content + trailing chevron-right. Full row is the interactive target — no button.

intent.Default: No fill, no stroke — inherits parent surface. Use inside bordered containers.
intent.Outline: color/surface/default fill + color/border/default stroke + radius/lg. Standalone card-like boundary.
intent.Muted: color/surface/muted fill + radius/lg, no stroke. Subtle tint for alternating/highlighted rows.

Image.fill: IMAGE fill — replace with actual src in implementation

Header.notes: Replace with real cover image in implementation

structure.Default: H AUTO-LAYOUT: content (title + description) → action-slot (button INSTANCE)
structure.Icon: H AUTO-LAYOUT: placeholder icon (16×16) → content → action-slot
structure.Header: V AUTO-LAYOUT: header FRAME (full-width image, no padding) → content-row → content
structure.Link: H AUTO-LAYOUT, TOP alignment: content → action-slot (chevron icon, no button)

composition.linkAlignmentNote: Type=Link uses counterAxisAlignItems=MIN (top) to anchor chevron to title when description wraps.
composition.actionSlotVisibility: Show when item has a discrete action. Hide for Type=Link (row is the action). Hide for Type=Header. Hide for read-only rows.
composition.descriptionVisibility: Optional — hide when items are atomic (command palettes, simple pickers, dense Xs lists).
composition.imageFills: Type=Image media and Type=Header header use muted fill as placeholder in Figma. Replace with actual images in implementation.

interactionModels.discreteAction: Types Default, Icon, Avatar, Image, Header — row itself is non-interactive; action-slot button is the sole target.
interactionModels.fullRowAction: Type=Link — wrap in <a> or <button>; entire row handles click/tap; no separate button.

keyboard: Tab to focus action-slot button (or full row for Type=Link)
behavior.noBuiltInState: item has no hover, focus, active, or selected state built in. Hover treatment is parent-level (e.g. row background to color/surface/accent — the Type=Link variant applies this directly via hover:bg-[var(--color-surface-accent)]).

accessibility.TypeLink: Wrap in <a href='...'> or <button> — gives accessible role and focus target.
accessibility.actionSlot: Button label must be descriptive with context, not just 'Edit' alone.
accessibility.TypeImage: Provide alt text: alt='Product: Blue Widget'.
accessibility.TypeHeader: Provide alt or aria-hidden='true' for decorative cover images.
accessibility.TypeAvatar: Avatar component exposes name via aria-label or visible text.

constraints: Type=Link: wrap entire row in <a> or <button>.
Type=Header has no action-slot — place actions outside the component if needed.
Do not override fills inside action-slot — change the button variant prop.
Variant=Outline inside a container that already has a border creates a double-border — use Variant=Default instead.
Use Type by what the leading element communicates, not aesthetics.
Description should add context the title doesn't carry — role, date, status, count.

useCases: Navigation menus where each row lists a destination with an icon and label
Activity feeds showing who performed an action, with a timestamp or status in the description
Settings lists inside a card — each row is a toggle, disclosure, or option
File or folder browsers with a thumbnail, filename, and file size on each row
Team or member group lists showing user avatars, names, and roles
Command palettes or search result lists where each result is a compact, tappable row

Type=Default.whenToUse: No leading media needed — text alone is sufficient to identify the item

Type=Icon.whenToUse: Items map to a recognisable category, action type, or feature

Type=Avatar.whenToUse: Each item represents a person or user entity

Type=Image.whenToUse: Each item represents a product, file, brand, or visual entity

Type=Header.whenToUse: Item needs a large cover image — editorial or feature-rich content

Type=Link.whenToUse: The entire row navigates somewhere — no discrete button action needed

Variant=Default.whenToUse: Item is inside a bordered list container or card that already defines boundaries
examples: Rows inside a panel with its own border

Variant=Outline.whenToUse: Item stands alone on open canvas or needs its own card-like boundary
examples: Items placed directly on page background

Variant=Muted.whenToUse: Subtle row tint for alternating rows, highlighted active state, or sidebar context

Size=Default.whenToUse: Standard density — comfortable reading with full description line

Size=Sm.whenToUse: Compact density — secondary panels, sidebars, nested lists

Size=Xs.whenToUse: Maximum density — very tight spaces or mobile views

comparedTo.situation: A single repeatable row in a vertical list
A self-contained block of independent information (metric, product, profile)
Many rows of uniform structured data with column headers and sorting
A navigation row that opens a new view when tapped
A full app navigation panel with grouped sections

notes: item is a custom design system component — no direct shadcn equivalent. Implementation is a custom React component.
Type=Header and Type=Link only have Variant=Default in smaller sizes (Sm/Xs).

changelog.change: Fixed token-ladder mismatch: container fill, title/description text, leading/trailing icon strokes, Header placeholder fill, and Link hover state were all bound to color/background/* (page-level ladder). Item is a component-level surface (list row, like Card), so rebound to color/surface/* equivalents: Outline fill → surface/default, Muted fill → surface/muted, title → surface/default/foreground, description → surface/muted/foreground, icon strokes → surface/default/foreground, Header placeholder → surface/muted, Link hover → surface/accent. Fixed in Figma (65:815, 243 bindings across 54 variants), item.meta.json, Item.md, item.tsx, and Item.stories.tsx.

darkMode.notes: No known dark mode differences — all tokens are semantic and mode-aware. The color/surface/* ladder (now used throughout) has correct Dark-mode values as of the 2026-06-15 dark mode pass.
